articles.headline: Wembanyama, Harper lead Spurs to 10th straight win, 124-119 over Bulls
articles.description: — Victor Wembanyama scored 32 points, Dylan Harper had 18 points, 10 assists and four steals and the San Antonio Spurs won their 10th straight game, overcoming a 22-point deficit to beat the Chicago Bulls 124-119 on Wednesday night.
articles.headlineJa: ウェンバニャマとハーパーが牽引し、スパーズがブルズに124-119で勝利し10連勝を飾る
articles.descriptionJa: ヴィクター・ウェンバニャマが32得点を挙げ、ディラン・ハーパーが18得点、10アシスト、4スティールを記録。サンアントニオ・スパーズは水曜夜の試合で22点差を跳ね返し、シカゴ・ブルズに124-119で勝利して10連勝を達成した。
articles.body:
CHICAGO -- — Victor Wembanyama scored 32 points, Dylan Harper had 18 points, 10 assists and four steals and the San Antonio Spurs won their 10th straight game, overcoming a 22-point deficit to beat the Chicago Bulls 124-119 on Wednesday night.


              The Bulls have lost eight in a row to fall to 1-9. They are 0-4 at home.


              Wembanyana also had nine rebounds and five blocks two days after his 40-point outburst in a win over the Phoenix Suns as the Spurs closed out a 4-0 trip. DeAaron Fox added 17 points and nine assists.


              Jalen Smith tied his career high with 23 points for the Bulls, and Nic Claxton had 17 off the bench.


              Bulls first-round pick Caleb Wilson scored 15 points in 15 minutes before leaving with a right hand injury in the third quarter. Wilson’s college season was cut short last winter by a pair of hand injuries.


              The Bulls led 64-42 midway through the second quarter, their biggest lead of the season, thanks to a 10-for-12 start from 3-point range. Chicago scored 41 points in the first quarter and shot 66% in the first half.


              The Spurs opened the third quarter with an 18-3 run to wipe out the Bulls' lead, enabled by five Chicago turnovers, then took control with an 11-2 run in the fourth quarter.


              Norman Powell, the Bulls' second-leading scorer, missed his second straight game with back spasms. Spurs guard Devin Vassell sat out his second in a row because of adductor tightness.


              Up next
              Spur: Host Golden State on Friday night.


              Bulls: Host Atlanta on Friday night.


              ------

articles.headline: Stephen Curry exits vs. Rockets, ruled out with abdominal soreness
articles.description: Warriors star Stephen Curry was ruled out of Wednesday's game in Houston after injuring his right abdomen in the first quarter.
articles.headlineJa: ステフィン・カリー、ロケッツ戦で途中退場、腹部の違和感で欠場
articles.descriptionJa: ウォリアーズのスター選手、ステフィン・カリーは第1クォーターに右腹部を負傷し、水曜日にヒューストンで行われた試合を欠場した。
articles.body:
HOUSTON -- Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry was ruled out of Wednesday's game in Houston after injuring his right abdomen in the first quarter. Curry started grabbing at his side a few minutes into the game, attempting to play through the pain while sporadically looking over at the training staff.

With 7:22 left in the first quarter, Curry came off a Draymond Green screen and nailed a 28-foot 3, but yelled in pain after the release and signaled toward the bench.

The Warriors called timeout a couple possessions later and Curry, after a brief conversation with Warriors coach Steve Kerr, went to the locker room in obvious discomfort followed by Drew Yoder, a key member of the team's medical staff.

 

Curry remained in the locker room getting checked out to close the first quarter before the team officially ruled him out with right abdominal soreness early in the second quarter.

The Warriors were down 19-10 when Curry exited. After opening the season 0-3, they entered the night on an eight-game win streak, spurred by a surge from Curry, who is averaging 30.6 points in 28.6 minutes per game.

The Warriors next play the Spurs in San Antonio on Friday night.

articles.headline: 2027 NFL draft rankings: Jordan Reid's top 50 prospects, scouting reports
articles.description: Jordan Reid updated his rankings for the 2027 NFL draft class with 50 players -- including eight quarterbacks and an elite wide receiver prospect.
articles.headlineJa: 2027年NFLドラフトランキング：ジョーダン・リードが選ぶトップ50プロスペクトとスカウティングレポート
articles.descriptionJa: ジョーダン・リードが2027年NFLドラフト候補のランキングを更新し、8人のクォーターバックとエリート級のワイドレシーバー候補を含む50人の選手を選出した。
articles.body:
With the 2026 college football season in full swing, it's time to start stacking the top prospects in the 2027 NFL draft class, which begins on April 29 in Washington, D.C. I've been watching and evaluating these players for a couple of years in some instances, and these rankings are a compilation of my scouting (both on film and in person) and conversations I've been having with scouts and evaluators around the NFL.

We're going to start these rankings with 50 players, with scouting reports on the top 25, but this list will expand as the draft gets closer and closer. And these rankings will evolve -- some players will shoot up boards, others will fall and still more will ultimately return to school for another year. But this is how I currently see things in the 2027 class.

Let's get to it, starting with arguably the best wide receiver prospect of the past 15-20 years. Underclassmen are marked with an asterisk, and the top names at every position are listed at the bottom.

Jump to:

Rankings by position

1. Jeremiah Smith, WR, Ohio State*

Height: 6-4 | Weight: 222

Stats through Nov. 7: 69 receptions for 1,200 receiving yards (17.4 yards per catch) and 14 touchdowns

Smith could have All-Pro potential early in his NFL career as a true No. 1 receiver. He immediately changes the offensive outlook for the team that adds him. He is sure-handed and can glide past defenders with ease. And he's equally as capable of winning with strength at the catch point. Smith's change of direction in routes needs to become sharper, as he can take too many choppy steps when working back toward passers. But he is tough to stop when allowed to attack defenses vertically.

2. Leonard Moore, CB, Notre Dame*

Height: 6-2 | Weight: 197

Stats through Nov. 7: 16 tackles, five passes defensed, 43.8% completion percentage allowed

With excellent length, speed and technique, Moore is the prototypical cornerback prospect. His length and physicality allow him to excel when getting hands on receivers in press man coverage. He also has the awareness to identify and defend route concepts in zone coverage. Moore has the ball skills to match receivers, routinely tracking and attacking the ball out of the air. But he needs to improve his discipline and hand timing at the top of routes.

3. Dylan Stewart, Edge, South Carolina*

Height: 6-5 | Weight: 250

Stats through Nov. 7: 12 tackles, two sacks, 4.5 tackles for loss, three forced fumbles, 20% pressure rate

With a slender frame, Stewart has rare burst and closing speed as a pass rusher. That allows him to wreak havoc on twists and stunts, though the tools have yet to lead to high-end production at the college level. Stewart must also become more consistent with using his length and shedding against the run. 

4. Colin Simmons, Edge, Texas*

Height: 6-3 | Weight: 246

Stats through Nov. 7: 25 tackles, 10.5 sacks, 16 tackles for loss, two forced fumbles, one fumble recovery, 20.5% pressure rate

articles.headline: Veteran WR Keenan Allen feeling energized by trade to 49ers
articles.description: Keenan Allen said while he didn't expect to get traded, landing with a contending team in the 49ers has him feeling energized.
articles.headlineJa: ベテランWRキーナン・アレン、49ersへのトレードに意欲
articles.descriptionJa: キーナン・アレンは、トレードされるとは思っていなかったが、優勝争いをしている49ersに加入したことで活力を得ていると語った。
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- Wide receiver Keenan Allen was at the Indianapolis Colts facility Tuesday morning meeting with coach Shane Steichen when he was informed that he needed to see interim general manager Ed Dodds.

Unaware that his name was even involved in trade discussions, Allen soon learned that he'd been traded to the San Francisco 49ers in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round pick. From there, Allen hustled home, packed a bag and got on a plane, landing in the Bay Area a little past midnight.

On Wednesday, Allen woke up, took a physical at 5:45 a.m. and began acclimating himself to his new surroundings while taking note that overnight he'd gone from the AFC South basement with the 2-7 Colts to the NFC-leading Niners.

That sudden change in the trajectory of his season was enough to help him through a whirlwind first day in San Francisco.

"I get a little boost in the way I feel coming into the building," Allen said. "Just being a part of the guys, it's a hell of a locker room. Obviously, these guys have accomplished so much in the past years. ... I'm running on just pure energy right now."

 

For Allen, 34, the biggest adjustment will be learning the terminology of coach Kyle Shanahan's playbook. He said conceptually the scheme is familiar, but all the words are different. Still, when asked what he expects this week, Allen said, simply, "I expect to play."

Whether Allen is able to play out the rest of the season for his new team remains to be seen. He is still amid a legal investigation stemming from an Aug. 30 arrest on suspicion of two misdemeanor offenses of drunken driven in downtown Indianapolis.

In September, prosecutors filed charges against Allen for operating a vehicle with alcohol concentration equivalent to .15 blood alcohol level or more and operating a vehicle while intoxicated. According to a probable cause affidavit obtained by ESPN, Allen's blood alcohol level was .224, which triggered the first of those misdemeanor charges.

Sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter in September that Allen could be subject to a minimum three-game suspension from the NFL for the arrest -- with the possibility of it being longer due to the high levels of intoxication. As of Wednesday, there's no court date set for Allen, though there's a remote "attorney conference" slated for Dec. 7 as the next step in the process.

Shanahan said the Niners traded for Allen knowing that a suspension was possible and acknowledged Wednesday that it's still a potential outcome.

"We're just waiting," Shanahan said. "We know the league handles that. It could go either way, so waiting for them to say ... [A suspension] is still possible."

For his part, Allen said he could not comment on the situation because it is an ongoing legal matter. In the meantime, Allen is doing his best to settle in with the team he nearly joined as a free agent in the offseason.

articles.headline: Sources: Philip Rivers set to return to NC State, deal to be finalized Friday
articles.description: Philip Rivers is set to return to NC State, this time as head football coach, once its trustees finalizes his contract after a meeting Friday, sources said.
articles.headlineJa: 情報筋：フィリップ・リバースがNCステート大学に復帰へ、金曜日に契約最終合意の見込み
articles.descriptionJa: 情報筋によると、フィリップ・リバースは金曜日の理事会で契約が最終決定され次第、今度はヘッドコーチとしてNCステート大学に復帰する予定だという。
articles.body:
The NC State board of trustees is expected to finalize a contract Friday that will make former NFL quarterback Philip Rivers his alma mater's new head football coach, sources told ESPN on Wednesday.

The long-expected hiring of Rivers, who has never been a college coach but is one of the program's most revered former players, is expected to culminate after Friday's meeting, sources told ESPN.

Rivers, who played quarterback at NC State from 2000 to 2003, is in his sixth season as coach at St. Michael Catholic High School in Fairhope, Alabama. He built the program from ground up and guided the Cardinals to the state semifinals in 2024 and '25.

Sources said the 44-year-old had told NC State that he wanted to finish his current high school season, which ended Friday.

In the early stages of the search, Rivers emerged as the favorite to replace Dave Doeren, who was fired Oct. 24. Another former Wolfpack and NFL quarterback, Russell Wilson, was also in discussions about the position.

Rivers broke nearly every NC State and ACC record during his career, throwing for 13,484 yards with 95 touchdowns. He led the Wolfpack to four straight bowl games under the Chuck Amato, winning three of them. Amato died last month at 80 years old.

Rivers' son, Gunner, committed to play for NC State on Feb. 23. Ranked 168th in the SC Next 300, Gunner Rivers threw for 10,847 yards with 119 touchdowns at St. Michael before his high school career ended due to a knee injury. 

Philip Rivers played 17 seasons in the NFL, all but one with the Chargers, before retiring after the 2020 season. Last year, he came out of retirement to start three games for the Colts after starter Daniel Jones and backup Riley Leonard were hurt.

In January, Rivers interviewed for the Bills' head coaching vacancy but later removed himself from the search.

Information from ESPN's David Hale was used in this report.

articles.headline: Dolphins hopeful QB Malik Willis will be back this season
articles.description: Coach Jeff Hafley said Miami sees Malik Willis as its starter regardless of when he returns from his groin injury.
articles.headlineJa: ドルフィンズ、QBマリク・ウィリスの今シーズン中の復帰に期待
articles.descriptionJa: ジェフ・ハフレイ監督は、鼠径部の怪我からいつ復帰するかにかかわらず、マイアミはマリク・ウィリスをスターターとして考えていると述べた。
articles.body:
MIAMI GARDENS, Fla. -- The Miami Dolphins are hopeful quarterback Malik Willis will return this season after his mandated minimum four-game stay on injured reserve, coach Jeff Hafley said Wednesday, and Willis is expected to remain the team's starter upon his return.

Hafley said Willis' MRI showed his groin injury had progressed to his core and the Dolphins' medical team believed he "needed the rest." Willis will seek a second opinion on his injury this week to decide whether or not to undergo surgery, but the Dolphins still see him as their starter, regardless of when he returns.

"Our hope is that he'll be back after his four weeks, which in time, if healthy, he'll return," Hafley said. "But he will be the starter when healthy, when he does return. And again, you look back at Malik and you watch him in that last game and you could see it. He couldn't quite move the way he had done early in the year and he was gritting through it and he was toughing through it. He made some plays with his feet in that game to keep plays alive.

"But we want him to be healthy so he can play at a high level without risking further injury."

Willis received treatment on his groin in each of the past two weeks. It didn't limit his practice participation, but he was noticeably hobbled in last week's loss to the Detroit Lions and was held to single-digit rushing yards for the second game in a row.

With Willis sidelined, second-year quarterback Kyle McCord will get his first career start Sunday against the Indianapolis Colts.

The Dolphins traded for McCord from the Green Bay Packers in August after the former sixth-round pick led the NFL in passing touchdowns this preseason. Though McCord has primarily run the Dolphins' scout team at practice since his arrival, Hafley said McCord's preseason tape showed desirable traits.

"He's got a strong arm, stronger than you think. He sees it well. The ball comes out fast," Hafley said. "He's decisive. He's aggressive. ... Again, he does not have experience in this league and this league is very different, but he does have experience. He has played in a lot of games, but from when I watched him, he's thrown a lot of passes and he does have arm talent and the ball comes out quickly and it'll be interesting to see."

The Philadelphia Eagles took McCord in the sixth round of the 2025 NFL draft, after he threw for an FBS-leading 4,779 yards at Syracuse as a senior. He also spent three seasons at Ohio State, going 11-1 as a starter in 2023.

McCord said it is his big-game experience in college that gives him confidence heading into the biggest week of his NFL career to date.

"It's a blessing, but I think once you get the first play, put on the helmet and get going, I think it'll feel just like football," McCord said of his opportunity. articles.headline: Source: Ravens, now on third kicker, sign journeyman Riley Patterson
articles.description: The Raven signed journeyman kicker Riley Patterson after his workout for the team on Wednesday, according to NFL Network.
articles.body:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- In the Ravens' most volatile season with kickers, Baltimore signed journeyman Riley Patterson after his workout for the team on Wednesday, a source told NFL Network's Mike Garafolo.

Patterson, 27, was cut by the Miami Dolphins on Oct. 20 after going 7-of-9 on field goals this season and struggling on kickoffs.

This marks the first time in the Ravens' 31-year history that they've used three kickers in a single season. Baltimore placed Tyler Loop (groin) on injured reserve on Nov. 3 and then had Jake Moody signed off its practice squad by the Atlanta Falcons on Tuesday.

 

Moody hit a 53-yard field goal in a 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday, but he chose to go to Atlanta, where he has the opportunity to play his home games indoors.

"Moody had a chance to be here," Ravens coach Jesse Minter said. "He had a choice to make and went somewhere else, [and I'll] leave it at that."

Patterson earned a spot with Baltimore by beating out a group of free agent kickers, which included Harrison Mevis. The Ravens will need Patterson for at least three more games while Loop is on injured reserve.

This is the 10th NFL team for Patterson, who has previously been with the Minnesota Vikings, New England Patriots, Detroit Lions, Jaguars, Cleveland Browns, Washington Commanders, New York Jets, Falcons, Dolphins and Ravens.

In his six-year career, Patterson has made 97-of-112 field goals (86.6%), which ranks 12th among kickers with at least 50 attempts since 2021. He is 7-of-14 from 50 yards or longer.

Patterson will kick for the Ravens on Monday night, when they host the winless Los Angeles Chargers.

articles.headline: Sources: Man United contact U.S. Soccer over Poch; Carrick meeting Thursday
articles.description: Manchester United have made contact with U.S. Soccer ahead of triggering Mauricio Pochettino's $10 million release clause as they close on a deal to hire the USMNT manager to replace Michael Carrick, sources told ESPN.
articles.headlineJa: 関係者によると：マンU、ポチェッティーノ獲得に向け米国サッカー協会に接触。カリックとの面会は木曜日
articles.descriptionJa: 関係者がESPNに語ったところによると、マンチェスター・ユナイテッドは、マイケル・カリックの後任として米国代表監督のマウリシオ・ポチェッティーノを獲得するため、1,000万ドルの契約解除条項を発動する前段階として、米国サッカー協会に接触した。
articles.body:
Manchester United have made contact with U.S. Soccer ahead of triggering Mauricio Pochettino's $10 million release clause as they close on a deal to hire the USMNT manager to replace Michael Carrick, sources told ESPN.

Sources added that executives from Man United are set to meet with Carrick on Thursday -- with the expectation that the 45-year-old will be relieved of his duties -- as the club pushes ahead with plans to hire Pochettino.

It will likely cost United another $2 million to hire Pochettino's staff, including long-time assistant Jesus Perez.

United executives including CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason WIlcox met with minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco on Wednesday ahead of their Thursday meeting with Carrick.

Carrick signed a two-year contract in May, but has overseen a poor start to the season. United have won just one Premier League game -- against newly-promoted Ipswich in August -- and sit 18th in the table.

The club have so far remained tight-lipped about the future of former United star player Carrick, who was at Carrington on Wednesday to lead training with the players not currently on international duty.

Pochettino is preparing for two USMNT games against Haiti, one on Nov. 14 and another on Nov. 17, in the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals.

A source told ESPN that U.S. Soccer said it expects Pochettino to oversee the two games against Haiti, the first for the Americans since winning all four matches during the Sept./Oct. international window.

Pochettino has extensive Premier League experience after spells at Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. He was considered for the United job before in 2018, 2022 and 2024.

United's next fixture is against Liverpool at Anfield on Nov. 22.

Trending rumors

- Bayern Munich are still in talks to sign Liverpool's teenage winger Rio Ngumoha, as reported by Bild's Christian Falk. Bayern were willing to pay €70 million to land the 18-year-old during the summer as they looked for a left winger who could complement Luis Díaz, before they went on to sign Ismael Saibari. But Bayern still need a left winger and could still look to land the England international in either January or the summer transfer window.

- Brentford center back Nathan Collins has been added to Manchester United's list of defensive options for the January transfer window, as reported by The Daily Mail. The versatile 20-year-old has played just 114 minutes this season and the Gunners are looking for attacking reinforcements on the wing following Bukayo Saka's injury. The Brazil international is one of a number of options being offered to Premier League clubs, but Diario AS has suggested there will be competition from AS Roma and Sporting CP, who both want to take Endrick on loan.

- In addition to referencing Endrick, The Independent has suggested Arsenal are also looking at Atlético Madrid's Álex Baena, RB Leipzig's Antonio Nusa and AFC Bournemouth's Junior Kroupi as they aim to sign a winger. With Real Madrid, Atlético and Chelsea all interested in central midfielder Martín Zubimendi, the Gunners would use the funds from any departure to sign a wide man.

- AC Milan are already making a move for Club Brugge striker Nicolò Tresoldi in January and want to pair him with Gonçalo Ramos, as reported by Gazzetta dello Sport. articles.headline: Schmeichel blasts Man United's 'disrespectful' treatment of Carrick amid Pochettino links
articles.description: Peter Schmeichel has criticised Manchester United for their "disrespectful" treatment of Michael Carrick as the club continue to be linked with Mauricio Pochettino.
articles.body:
Peter Schmeichel has criticised Manchester United for their "disrespectful" treatment of Michael Carrick as the club continue to be linked with Mauricio Pochettino.

Pochettino is the leading candidate to replace Carrick as head coach and the club have opened talks with the 54-year-old's representatives, sources also told ESPN.

But former United goalkeeper Schmeichel believes the problems at the club stem from above Carrick, and that the under-pressure boss should get the chance to bring in his own players when the January transfer window opens.

"I absolutely do feel sympathy for him. I think the way this is playing out is very disrespectful to him," Schmeichel told 'The Overlap Daily.'

"If I'm honest, I don't think he's doing anything wrong. I know the team that he's in charge of is where they are in the table, but I don't put all of that on him.

"There are so many things that have been going on at Manchester United literally since Sir Alex [Ferguson] and David Gill left the club. And it's never been corrected.

"It's not been the correct people, not the right people in charge, and slowly it's just gone worse.

"And if you think about this transfer window now, it's abundantly clear to everyone -- everyone who knows just a little bit about football -- that Manchester United needed defenders.

"They got through a whole transfer window without signing a single defender. You can't win games if you concede 30 goals in 10 games ... that was not addressed.

"So yes, I do feel a lot of sympathy for Michael. I think what is happening is wrong. I think we should stick with Michael.

- Man United near Mauricio Pochettino deal, Michael Carrick awaits verdict - sources

- USMNT or Manchester United: Pros and cons of Pochettino's options

"I think we should just try and steady the ship a little bit and then get into January and then sign the players that he feels he needs to bring the team forward and then be realistic about what this season is all about ..."

Pochettino enjoyed great success at Tottenham, leading them to the 2019 Champions League final.

One of his star players there, England captain Harry Kane, paid tribute to his former coach on Wednesday.

"Me and Mauricio obviously have a fantastic relationship," he said. "I mentioned him as one of the coaches who had a big impact on my career and definitely my development at that stage in my career.

"I needed his guidance. The way he pushed me, not just on the pitch but off the pitch as well was really, really helpful.

"Obviously a fantastic coach, he's managed the biggest clubs in the world. From my point of view, I can't speak highly enough of him. We'll have to wait and see what happens but I know he's a great guy and also a fantastic manager."

Information from PA contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Why Messi won't be 'doing a Wrexham' as owner of Cornellà
articles.description: UE Cornellà gained global fame when Lionel Messi purchased them earlier this year. Why has the GOAT bought a semi-professional club in Spain's fifth tier?
articles.body:
BARCELONA -- Last month, a club owned by Lionel Messi beat Manchester City, Inter Milan and Arsenal to reach the final of a prestigious cup competition. This did not happen in a game of Football Manager, or EA FC. It actually happened. UE Cornellà, the tiny team from Spain's fifth tier, went up against the best in the world and beat them.

The twist is that it was not the first team. At the same time as Cornellà's under-16 side were beating Arsenal in Miami in the Messi Cup, the senior side were having a much less glamorous afternoon back in a drizzly Barcelona.

A second-half strike from Marc Esteban earned a point for Ignasi Senabre's side against FE Grama in Spanish soccer's semi-professional fifth tier. But it did little to improve on what has been a disappointing season so far for the club taken over in April by former Argentina and Barcelona star Messi.

Messi's takeover prompted talk, admittedly outside of Cornellà circles, of 'doing a Wrexham.' The term is a nod to the Welsh side's rapid rise through the English football pyramid, from non-league to within one promotion of the Premier League, under Hollywood stars Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac.

"The comparison is understandable because in both cases there is a world-famous figure involved," a source at the Catalan club tells ESPN. "But they are very different projects, contexts and models. Each club has its own project."

So what does Messi want Cornellà to become? Is the ambition to take the first team up to LaLiga, or does he see greater potential in the academy and the community?

Messi's Cornellà takeover shocked everyone

Cornellà coach Senabre initially thought the announcement regarding Messi was a hoax.

"I found out via the press," Senabre tells ESPN. "All of a sudden everyone was talking about it, but before then it hadn't come out anywhere. I thought it was AI at first."

Next thing Senabre knew, he was ushered into a meeting room at the club's modest stadium, which doubles as their training ground. The Camp Municipal de Cornellà sits literally in the shadows of neighbouring LaLiga club Espanyol's RCDE Stadium. The two grounds are separated by a 10-metre-wide walkway in Cornellà de Llobregat on the southern outskirts of Barcelona, where Messi spent 20 years of his life.

There, alongside his staff and the players, he watched a five-minute introduction video sent by Messi. The introduction, of course, was hardly necessary. Everyone knew who Messi was, but a source says it's an example of how involved he has been from the start.

articles.headline: Fantasy football matchup ranks: Upgrade Ollie Gordon II, downgrade Jordan Love
articles.description: The most and least favorable matchups in the NFL for this week's games at the four key fantasy positions.
articles.body:
Making tough lineup decisions each week can be the most challenging part of the fantasy football process. When you're torn between two similar players and simply don't know which to start, start the player with the superior matchup.

Ah, but exactly how does one determine the best (and worst) weekly matchups?

The matchup rankings provide a schedule independent method to evaluate positional matchups each week, ranking opposing defenses in order of most to least favorable for opposing players at all four skill positions. Instead of relying upon seasonal totals, we calibrate points-allowed data to show how each defense fared relative to the difficulty of the schedule it has faced over the past five weeks. 

"Adj. FPA," or Adjusted Fantasy Points Allowed, reflects how far above or below players' weekly PPR fantasy point averages that defense held opponents at that position. A positive number means that the matchup is favorable; a negative number means it is unfavorable. Additionally, remember that teams often use multiple running backs and wide receivers in a game, and these plus/minus averages cover all of a team's personnel at that position.

Finally, a caveat: Matchups are only one ingredient in my rankings formula. Not every favorable matchup should be exploited, nor unfavorable matchup avoided. If you want the most complete source for whom to start and sit each week, consult our weekly rankings.

Matchups highlight: Trevor Lawrence, Jacksonville Jaguars (at Tennessee Titans). He hasn't been needed to do a whole lot in blowout victories the past two weeks, averaging 16.5 fantasy points in games his Jaguars won by 35 and 23 points. The worry here is that the game script might fall along similar lines, what with the Jaguars favored by 10.5 points. Nevertheless, this is too good a matchup to ignore, for a quarterback whose team is rolling recently and who was one of the position's best during the second half of 2025. The Titans surrendered 18.22 and 39.48 fantasy points to Deshaun Watson and Joe Burrow in their prior two games. Lawrence also scored 20-plus points in both meetings with the Titans in 2025, and two of his four career 30-plus-point games have come against the division rival.

articles.headline: How Harry Kane rose to win Ballon d'Or and became an England legend
articles.description: Harry Kane went from overlooked youngster to Ballon d'Or winner. Now he's about to become England's record appearance-holder -- and possibly their greatest-ever player.
articles.body:
Another week, another landmark moment for Harry Kane. Life is like that right now for the England captain, who will become his country's all-time record appearance-maker when leading out the Three Lions against Croatia on Thursday.

It completes a remarkable fortnight for Kane, 33, after he won the men's Ballon d'Or for the first time and signed a new contract with Bayern Munich through to 2029. He is now one of the highest-paid players in Europe, at more than €30 million per year.

Surpassing Peter Shilton's 125-cap England record felt almost impossible for more than three decades, especially for an outfield player. Wayne Rooney reached 120, David Beckham 115, Steven Gerrard 114 and Ashley Cole 107, but Kane will go clear on his own with years still ahead of him.

- Kane's long road to Ballon d'Or glory ends with crowning moment

- USMNT or Manchester United: Pros and cons of Pochettino's options

- Why Messi won't be 'do a Wrexham' as owner of non-league Cornellà

England's goal-scoring record appeared a similarly difficult climb. Sir Bobby Charlton's tally of 49 stood for 45 years before Rooney reached the half-century in 2015 and later ended on 53. Kane is on a remarkable 91 -- and counting.

He has captained England more often than any other player in history, leading England to back-to-back European Championship finals and a third-place finish at this summer's World Cup, the men's national team's best placing since their sole 1966 triumph.

The only thing missing is a major international trophy, something he willingly admits he would trade every individual accolade to have. But Kane's case for becoming England's greatest-ever player grows with each passing season.

After ending his 19-year association with Premier League club Tottenham Hotspur, Kane joined Bundesliga giants Bayern Munich for €120 million in August 2023. In March of that year, Bayern appointed Thomas Tuchel as manager. Former sporting director Hasan Salihamidžić has publicly claimed the club decided on Kane as their top summer target around a month later having first considered him in late 2021.

"He took convincing, but don't forget Bayern Munich is a huge club with a big reputation," Tuchel, now Kane's manager with England, told ESPN. "The prospect of winning titles, the prospect of competing in the Champions League every year, quarterfinals, semifinals, finals in basically all competitions gave us a good hand.

"But still, it is a big step for the English captain to step out of the Premier League and then the language is not easy. So it was a big step out of his comfort zone for Harry.

"In the end, with hindsight, because we are all smarter, it seems to have brought out the very, very best in him. He adapted so quickly, he became such an influential figure in such a big club. Full credit to him and his family. He took convincing, but we felt from the start it was possible."

articles.headline: Arsenal's Martin Zubimendi denies wanting to leave amid Atlético Madrid links
articles.description: Martín Zubimendi has denied he is considering leaving Arsenal in the January transfer window amid reported interest from Atlético Madrid.
articles.body:
Martín Zubimendi has denied he is considering leaving Arsenal in the January transfer window amid reported interest from Atlético Madrid.

The Spanish midfielder has logged only 100 minutes in seven league appearances for Arsenal this term, a far cry from last season, where he played in all 38 Premier League games to help the Gunners win the title, averaging 79 minutes per game.

"I realise the winter transfer window is coming up, and rumours may start to circulate," he told Marca while on international duty with Spain.

"I've also read that a move [to Atlético] might be on the cards, but that's far from the case. I haven't wasted any energy on it, nor have I got in touch with anyone. I haven't wasted any energy on external matters. I've got enough on my plate just trying to earn a place in the team, get some playing time and fight to win this Premier League title, which is looking so promising."

Arsenal are top of the Premier League, five points clear of nearest rivals Brighton.

Asked if he will continue at Arsenal until the end of the season, Zubimendi, whose contract runs until June 2030, said: "Yes, I hope so. I'm happy there. I'm happy in London."

A 2026 World Cup winner with Spain, Zubimendi believes the workload of last season that led to physical fatigue, has affected his performances.

"I played an enormous number of minutes [last season], and, to be honest, I was tired," he said. "There were other factors, too, but the physical aspect could very well have been one of them."

Asked if he has considered seeking psychological help to deal with this bad patch, Zubimendi said: "I've thought about it and wouldn't rule it out, but for now, I haven't gone down that path.

"I'm well, I'm calm and happy with how I'm handling this situation. It's something I'd never experienced before, and I think you learn from situations like this too. What's more, it's at times like this that you need the people around you the most, and they're there for you."

Zubimendi, 27, is focusing on the positives.

"When you've been playing a lot of minutes and your role changes to playing less, I'm managing to see the bright side," he said. "I think everything comes and goes; just as the opposite happened to me last year and I played practically every minute, things can change very quickly."

Zubimendi admits he was warned by Arsenal coach Mikel Arteta that the he would face competition for playing time with the arrival of midfielder Bruno Guimarães.

"I spoke to Mikel [Arteta] at the start of the season," Zubimendi said.

articles.headline: Dirk Kuyt leaves Fenerbahce a week after defeating Liverpool
articles.description: Dirk Kuyt left Fenerbahce on Wednesday, one week after guiding the team as interim coach to beat his old club Liverpool in the Champions League.
articles.body:
ISTANBUL -- Dirk Kuyt left Fenerbahce on Wednesday, one week after guiding the team as interim coach to beat his old club Liverpool in the Champions League.

The former Netherlands forward took charge of that 3-2 win in Istanbul despite the club already having made a deal with Emre Belözoğlu to take over.

Kuyt returned in July to Fenerbahce, where he played from 2012-15, to assist coach Ismail Kartal who resigned last month.

"We thank you from the bottom of our hearts for all that you have contributed to these colors," Fenerbahce said in a social media post announcing Kuyt's exit. "Today we say goodbye to you but your place in this big family will never change."

Belözoğlu, a former captain of the club, takes over a team sixth in the Turkish league and 19th in the 36-team Champions League standings.

Fenerbahce's next Champions League opponent is Shakhtar Donetsk in London on Nov. 25.
